Puerto Nariño · Colombian Amazon

Lake Tarapoto & dolphin watching

Follow the waterways in search of river dolphins and the quiet beauty of the lakes.

Ask Amaru on WhatsApp ↗

About this experience

Explore Lake Tarapoto by day, with time for the waterside landscapes and the search for river dolphins. This experience centres on the lake and its wildlife, rather than paddling or forest trails. Dolphins live in the wild, so each outing is different and sightings are never guaranteed.

Lake Tarapoto belongs to a network of lakes, rivers and creeks near Puerto Nariño, in the Colombian Amazon. Recognised as a Wetland of International Importance under the Ramsar Convention, the complex is a habitat for river dolphins, fish and birds. Looking beyond a single sighting reveals a landscape in which water connects many forms of life.

Take time to notice the shoreline, the reflections and the activity around the water. A dolphin may be the moment you hope for, while the wider lake landscape gives the outing its character. Let the search remain patient and respectful: wild animals choose where they go, and each visit unfolds differently.

Destination context sources: Ramsar ↗

What to explore

  • River and lake landscapes
  • Dolphin watching when conditions allow
  • Meeting point and duration confirmed together

What should I confirm?

Ask about the route, departure, group requirements, guide language, equipment, transport and what is included. Share your dates and number of travellers, and review the full price and cancellation conditions before confirming anything.

Routes depend on water levels, weather and local conditions. Wildlife sightings cannot be guaranteed.
